pilot.summary: First game ever with the deck, a pod of three at home against Stuart (zombie tokens) and Steven (card draw and counterspells). Sol Ring in the opener got it going fast, and a late wheel made Shabraz big enough that I almost killed Stuart with commander damage. Then it went grindy. Brallin got removed twice and picked up tax, no more ramp showed up, and I had no removal for the board or answer to Steven's counters. No result was logged.

A loss at Oliver's, the second game of the night, against Oliver, Tom and Ryan. I mulliganed into a hand with one playable creature and a bunch of wheels and wasn't sure I should have kept it. The Shabraz wheels went well. My main finding was that the list ran too many wheels. They should be finishers, held until both commanders are out and big, partly because the table doesn't like discarding its hand over and over.

A short note on the first game with the voltron list, v2.0.0. It was slow: no removal, slow to get cards out, and mana starved for a round. I couldn't tell if it was sequencing or the cards I saw. No result or table was logged.

A loss at Ryan's house to Alex's warp deck, which ramps to around 15 mana and keeps its warped creatures with an artifact that ends the turn. Ryan was on Slivers. The draw/discard engine ran well and Smothering Tithe made steady Treasure, but I kept a land-and-ramp hand with one wheel, held both commanders back waiting for a wheel that never came, and got outpaced. The rule since is to cast the first commander on curve.

A late three-player loss at my house. Alex played my Goblin Storm and won on Purphoros pings, and David was on golems. I kept a ramp-heavy hand again, got Marauding Mako to +6/+6 off a wheel, but never got a commander out. I put it on piloting: I got distracted by the small discard creatures instead of building toward the commanders.

Second game of a five-player night at Oliver's, at a table that had stepped up to bracket 4. Ryan's T'Vol went infinite around turn 8-9 and won. I had Shabraz, Brallin, Fiery Emancipation, Smothering Tithe with 36 Treasure, Mystic Remora and Teferi's Ageless Insight out, plus a tutor for Shark Typhoon in hand, but never drew a wheel. I dug 9-10 cards and found nothing, and the wheels were deep. I asked for research only, no swaps off one game.

First game on the newly sleeved v2.3.0. I found the wheels, got the commanders big and could have won. It still felt clunky and slow, brittle with nine mana and two taxes for the commanders, and the draw-and-discard was laborious. No result or table was logged.

Third game of an 0-3 night at Oliver's, the first on v3.0.0, against a bracket 3 table that is optimized to win around turn four. Oliver landed Krenko and the table asked me to kill it. I held Swords to Plowshares and a second removal spell, cast Shabraz instead, then passed another turn with mana open. Oliver went off for 30-plus damage in one turn. I called it entirely a piloting error, said it was the right hand misplayed, and asked for no deck changes.

Second game of a Thursday at Steven's: Steven on Magda, David on golems, Stuart on Rotcleaver zombies with Blood Artist. I mulliganed once, kept a land-heavy hand with no early creatures, missed a land drop and had no creature until about turn four, so everybody attacked me. Short of mana for Shabraz, I cast Brallin first. Jace's Archivist then wheeled the table under Smothering Tithe for 14 Treasure, Faerie Mastermind kept everyone drawing, Shabraz came down and swung 18 flying, trample at Steven into two 6/6 dragons, and 6 commander damage got through. I held the Treasure instead of casting the humans in hand, Steven swung back and left me at 1, and Stuart sacrificed a zombie on his end step and killed me with Wheel of Fortune in hand. A loss, but Shabraz did its thing and worked the table. I'm still asking whether swinging Brallin at Steven was a mistake.

read.what_it_does: On v3.0.0 it lands Shabraz, grows him off a wheel and card draw, and swings a big flying, trampling shark for commander damage. In 009 it did exactly that for the first time on this list. Jace's Archivist wheeled the table under Smothering Tithe for 14 Treasure, Faerie Mastermind kept the table drawing, Shabraz came down that turn and hit Steven for 18 with 6 commander damage through two 6/6 dragons (009). Brallin is the four-mana fallback now, not the main win line. He's a body on defense, and the discard cards still work through him (009). In 008 Shabraz resolved, but I lost to Krenko before the plan could show (008).
read.how_it_plays: Slow to start, then a real threat once Shabraz is out. In 009 I had no creature until about turn four, and then Shabraz did its thing and worked the table (009). Spare Treasure buys a choice: trample on the attack, or a mana to give a human flying and block (009). It pointed all its damage at one seat. Shabraz hurt Steven a lot and never aimed at Stuart or David, and Stuart took the win (009). Both games on this list were losses to something faster. Krenko did 30-plus in one turn at Oliver's, where the bracket 3 decks aim to win around turn four (008). In 009 I died at 1 life to Stuart's drain, one turn before a Wheel of Fortune comeback (009). On older lists I kept writing that it felt slow because the two commanders cost nine mana (003, 005, 007). Casting Brallin first when Shabraz's five isn't there is how 009 got around that (009). It survives wipes: on v2.2.0 it lived through several and lost to a combo, not damage (006). The table either loves the wheels or hates them (001, 002).
mindful_of: Spend the Treasure on the humans. In 009 I held it instead of casting the humans in hand. Steven swung back, I sacrificed Esper Sentinel and another human, blocked with Brallin and ended at 1. Shabraz can give them flying, so they block on a wide board (009).
Brallin is the four-mana fallback. When I'm short of mana for Shabraz, cast Brallin: he's a body on defense, and the discard cards in hand still work with him (009).

A land-heavy keep with no early creatures draws the whole table's attacks. In 009 I had no board until about turn four and everybody attacked me (009). On v2.2.0 I doubted ramp-heavy keeps in 004 and 005 too (004, 005).

Remove an opposing Blood Artist early. In 009 I left Stuart's on the table, every creature death drained the table and gained him life, and the last point that killed me came from a zombie sacrifice (009).

When the whole table names the threat and I'm holding the answer, use it. In 008 I held Swords to Plowshares and a second two-mana removal spell, cast Shabraz instead, and Krenko killed me for 30-plus. I called it entirely a piloting error (008).
Kill on sight at Oliver's: Krenko (Oliver) and Purphoros (Tom). Early artifact removal on a Sol Ring opener is a fair play at that table (008). Purphoros also won 005 (005).
Open question from 009: was swinging Brallin at Steven a mistake? Steven blocked with two and lost a dragon, but Brallin was the blocker I needed when Steven swung back (009).
Cast the first commander on curve. On v2.2.0 I held both back to dodge a wipe, waited for a wheel that never came, and lost the tempo (004).

The wheel can be the missing piece. On v2.2.0 the board was set up with 36 Treasure, I dug 9-10 cards, and the first wheel was deep in the library (006). Know what the tutors fetch when there's no wheel.
Don't fire a wheel just to fire it. In 001 I threw away useful cards of my own because I just needed to do the wheel (001). Wheels hit hardest as finishers with the commanders out and big (002, 009).

Discarding without drawing back strands a small hand (005), and forced discard felt like a cost and laborious on older lists (006, 007). v3.0.0 cut loot pieces, and neither game on it names this as a drag (008, 009).
Commander tax piles up. Brallin was removed twice in 001 even with protection out (001). Swiftfoot Boots, which protected them then, is back in v3.0.0 (001).
Wheels cost goodwill. Making people discard their hand over and over is not something they enjoy (001, 002).
Downweight the goldfish on this deck. It doesn't see removal or interaction, and following it moves the deck in the wrong direction (002).
read.what_changed: v3.0.0 (Shabraz-first, merged and sleeved 2026-11-10) cut the wheel-and-burn engine from v2.3.0, including Marauding Mako, Glint-Horn Buccaneer, Psychosis Crawler and the loot spells. It added card draw to grow Shabraz, protection for when he lands (Swiftfoot Boots, Shelter, Slip Out the Back) and double strike. Two games on it now. 008 was a misplay and showed nothing about the list (008). 009 is the first real read: the draw grew Shabraz, he was a real threat, and I was happy with how the deck worked and how it piloted (009). That's one game against 007, where v2.3.0 felt clunky, slow and laborious even when it found its wheels (007). Brallin's job changed with this list. He's the fallback and still runs the discard engine, not the main win line (009). Neither game says the new protection was cast, so it's untested at the table (008, 009). Superseded lessons: the 'no removal' complaints in 001 and 003 were about lists before answers-v1 (v2.1.0) added interaction (001, 003). In 008 the removal was in hand and I didn't use it (008). The 'too many wheels' read in 002 was on v1.3.0, and v2.0.0 cut wheels after it (002). Mystic Remora and Embercleave from 006, the Ledger and Bonnie/Annie loot pieces from 004, and Marauding Mako and Lightning Greaves from 005 are on lists this deck no longer runs.
